chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whatever you doubt after you have finished your prayer, proceed (with what you are certain of) and do not return (to repeat it)."
ai.seo_question: What should one do if they doubt a part of their prayer after finishing it?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of 'stability of the certain' (istishab al-muqarrar) for doubts arising after the final taslim, distinguishing this phase from doubts during prayer. It instructs the worshipper to assume the prayer is complete and valid, preventing excessive doubt (waswas) from invalidating the act. This ruling is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for maintaining the integrity of congregational and individual prayers by avoiding unnecessary repetitions.
